concept.name: Quote currency
concept.definition: The second currency in a currency-pair quotation, i.e. the currency in which the price of one unit of the base currency is expressed. In EUR/USD 1.2500, USD is the quote (counter) currency and the rate states that 1 euro is exchanged for 1.25 US dollars.
concept.intuition: The quote currency is the 'money you pay with' in the pair — the quoted number is an amount of it.
concept.mechanics: The pair price Q is measured in quote-currency units per base-currency unit. Profit and loss on an FX position accrues in the quote currency and is then converted to the account currency; the quote currency's interest rate enters forward pricing through covered interest parity.
concept.formula: Quote-currency amount = base-currency amount x Q, where Q is the quoted pair rate.
concept.failure_modes: Confusing base and quote currencies inverts the meaning of an appreciation and of position P&L; the CCY1/CCY2 convention exists partly to remove this ambiguity.
concept.misconceptions: It is wrong to think the quote currency is 'always the dollar'; the dollar is the quote currency in EUR/USD but the base currency in USD/JPY.
concept.example: If EUR/USD rises from 1.2500 to 1.2600, it takes more of the quote currency (USD) to buy one euro, so the euro (base) has appreciated against the dollar (quote).
